title: Mouse Hunt
tagline: One mouse. Two brothers. Plenty of cheese.
about: Two brothers inherit a run-down mansion and a tiny mouse who refuses to leave.
cue: Serve the snacks when the brothers set their first mouse trap with cheese.
faces: I cooked for the mayor once, Lars, and look how that went. Eat before the mouse gets to it.
One mouse. Two brothers. Plenty of cheese.
String cheese, aged cheddar, gouda and blue with crackers, grapes and nuts.
Cheddar and gruyere grilled cheese cut in wedges with holes poked in the top.
Chicken breast stuffed with spinach and ricotta, mushroom cream sauce, potato gratin.
LaRue mansion pork loin with crackling
Getting the old LaRue mansion ready for auction.
Baked cream cheese cheesecake on a cookie crust, spread with lemon curd.
Honey vanilla milkshakes in small glasses, with a cheese cracker on each rim.

A tray charge applies to every order. Prices subject to change. Every drink is alcohol free. A crumbling mansion and Catzilla the cat. Caesar the exterminator and his bold methods. Form RS 497. Images: TMDB.

    StartersSmuntz string cheese boardString cheese, aged cheddar, gouda and blue with crackers, grapes and nutsHow to make it4 sticks of string cheese150g aged cheddar150g gouda100g blue cheese1 box water crackers300g green grapes50g mixed nutsCut the cheddar, gouda and blue cheese into wedges.Arrange the cheeses and string cheese on a wooden board with the crackers, grapes and a little bowl of nuts.Leave one small wedge of cheese on its own at the edge as bait.Mousetrap cheese toastiesCheddar and gruyere grilled cheese cut in wedges with holes poked in the topHow to make it8 slices of white bread40g butter, soft150g cheddar, grated150g gruyere, gratedButter the bread on the outside and fill with the cheddar and gruyere.Cook in a pan until golden and melting on both sides.Cut each into cheese-shaped wedges and poke a few holes in the top with a chopstick like cartoon cheese.Smuntz String spaghetti frittersTheir father's old string factoryHow to make itAs written, serves 4Tangles of spaghetti bound with egg, parmesan and parsley, fried into crisp golden nests and served with a smoky tomato and basil dipping sauce.Cook 200g spaghetti, drain and cool.Toss with 3 beaten eggs, 60g grated parmesan, chopped parsley and pepper.Heat 1cm oil in a frying pan and drop in twisted forkfuls, flattening slightly.Fry 2 minutes a side until crisp and golden.Simmer 300ml passata with a garlic clove, half a tsp smoked paprika and basil for 10 minutes to dip.Crispy fried school prawnsNo cockroaches. Ask the mayor.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsErnie's spinach ricotta stuffed chickenChicken breast stuffed with spinach and ricotta, mushroom cream sauce, potato gratinHow to make it4 chicken breasts100g baby spinach250g ricotta250g mushrooms, sliced20g butter600ml thickened cream1kg potatoes, thinly sliced2 tbsp oilWilt the spinach, squeeze dry and mix with the ricotta. Cut a pocket in each chicken breast and fill.Layer the potatoes in a dish with most of the cream and bake at 180°C.Sear the chicken in oil, then roast at 200°C alongside for the last 20 minutes.Cook the mushrooms in butter, add the remaining cream and simmer until thick. Serve over the chicken.LaRue mansion pork loin with cracklingGetting the old LaRue mansion ready for auctionHow to make itAs written, serves 4Pork loin rolled with sage and garlic, roasted with apples and potatoes until the crackling shatters, with a sharp apple and mustard sauce.Score the skin of a 1.5kg rolled pork loin, rub with salt and dry in the fridge for an hour.Push sage leaves and garlic slivers into the meat.Roast at 240°C for 25 minutes, then at 180°C for 1 hour with 1kg halved potatoes and 3 quartered apples.Simmer 2 more chopped apples with sugar and water until soft, then stir in 1 tsp Dijon.Rest the pork 10 minutes and carve.SweetsLaRue house lemon curd cheesecakeBaked cream cheese cheesecake on a cookie crust, spread with lemon curdHow to make it250g sweet biscuits, crushed100g butter, melted500g cream cheese150g caster sugar3 eggs4 tbsp lemon curdMix the crushed biscuits with the butter and press into a tin.Beat the cream cheese and sugar, then the eggs. Pour over the base.Bake at 160°C for 50 minutes, then cool in the oven. Chill until firm.Spread with lemon curd before serving.DrinksMouse-sized honey vanilla shakesHoney vanilla milkshakes in small glasses, with a cheese cracker on each rimHow to make it500ml cold milk4 scoops of vanilla ice cream2 tbsp honeyground cinnamon, a pinch8 round cheese biscuitsBlend the milk, ice cream, honey and cinnamon until thick and frothy.Pour into eight small glasses.
